newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A shares soar to close, led by bank.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares soar to close, led by bank.

text.p: Shenzhen's A shares powered ahead 6.73 percent on Friday, pushed up by a surge in market giant Shenzhen Development Bank Co and by investor optimism in the last week before the handover of Hong Kong to China, brokers said.

The bullish A share market also helped drag the foreign currency B share index up 2.52 points or 1.72 percent to close at 149.15 on turnover of HK$62 million compared with Thursday's HK$42 million, brokers said.
The A share index soared 28.37 points or 6.73 percent to 449.97, with turnover swelling to 9.3 billion yuan from 5.1 billion yuan in the previous session.

"Today's bull-run was led by heavyweight Shenzhen Development Bank, whose surprisingly strong performance underpinned investor confidence and sparked a wave of buying in a range of shares," Cheng Li, an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The bank powered ahead 3.09 yuan to its 10 percent limit-up at 33.96 yuan on volume of 24 million shares worth 784 million yuan, making it the second most actively traded stock.
Trading in the bank's shares had been suspended since last Friday as punishment for the bank's share trading irregularities and resumed today.

Last week, Beijing securities authorities announced it would sack the bank's president He Yun after the bank was found to have used bank funds to trade its own shares and would seize nearly 100 million yuan in profits from its illicit stock investment.
"The bank soared because news of its punishment had been factored into the share price," Xu Yinhui, another Guotai analyst said.
"Investors scrambled to buy the bank shares due to confidence in the company's earnings prospects," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
The bank's dividend plan for 1996, which consists of a five-for-10 bonus share issue and a cash payout of 0.2 yuan per share, also stirred buying interest, brokers said.
Shenzhen Development Bank, China's only bank with a domestic exchange listing, is considered as an A share leader due to the large size of its capitalisation and robust earnings record.
The bank led a bull-run in Shenzhen's A share market between January and May this year before giving up some gains due to an official investigation into its share trading.
Brokers also said investors poured funds into A shares in expectation of sustained rises in the final days before the Hong Kong handover at midnight on June 30.

"Anyway, people do not expect Beijing to announce any new anti-speculation measures next week, which is such an important time for the central government," an analyst at Jardine Fleming Securities in Shenzhen said.
"B shares are poised to do better next week," the analyst added.
Beijing started to crack down on the nation's overheated stock markets last month, stopping a five-month bull-run dead in its tracks.
In the B share market, Chengming Paper put in the strongest performance, rising HK$0.46 or 7.08 percent to HK$6.96.
